name: Hamilton Live - Calendar
notes: Set up as a backstop for venues with unreliable email alerts, per Dan. Confirmed live 2026-09-19 via Claude-for-Chrome DOM inspection - fully server-rendered, semantic markup, no JS gap. Extractor cross-validated two independent ways against the real live page before commit (a DOM query walk and the exact regex-chunking approach the extractor uses, both run in-browser) - both agreed exactly, 48 events. No off-profile pre-filter defined - general-purpose venue with a genuinely mixed bill, no free negative-signal marker the way Blues Alley's own genre-series labels serve as one; untracked bookings go straight to score_candidates.py. Given real booking volume, expect some [filtered] noise most weeks even in steady state - working as intended, not a broken watch.

name: JVs Restaurant - Calendar Flyer
notes: Calendar is posted as flyer images with no extractable text - OCR is out of scope for this system. The venue's own filename convention embeds the month (JV_NEW_FLYER_DESIGN_<MONTH>_<YEAR>_...), confirmed via plain fetch 2026-09-19; a live-browser DOM query shows something different (client-side JS swaps the image to inline base64 post-load) but that JS never runs in a headless fetch, so it does not affect this. Goal is deliberately coarse - nudge Dan to go look, not extract show data. The mail body shows the old/new image URLs; the month is visible right in the filename. ignore_contains excludes the venue's static "how to book us" flyer (JV_BOOKING.jpg) on the same page, which is unrelated and would otherwise fire a false alert if it ever changed. It also excludes the static food photo Best_burgers.jpg for the same reason. Taste-profile matches at this venue (JP Soars, Gabe Stillman, Albert Castiglia) are underplays among open-mic/cover-band bookings - this watch cannot see which month has one, only that a new month went up; the actual check is still manual.
